target.title: fix(openai): add handshakeTimeout to realtime voice WebSocket
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The OpenAI realtime voice WebSocket creates `new WebSocket()` without `handshakeTimeout`. The `ws` library defaults this to 0 (unlimited).

The bridge-level `connectTimeout` watchdog (`setTimeout → ws.terminate()`) catches stalls AFTER `open` fires (session not configured), but does NOT protect against a TCP peer that accepts the connection and stalls the HTTP upgrade — `ws` never emits `open` in that case, and `ws.terminate()` on a CONNECTING socket may not clean up underlying TCP resources. The `handshakeTimeout` operates at the ws library level and directly bounds the upgrade handshake.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `handshakeTimeout: OpenAIRealtimeVoiceBridge.CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` (10 s) to the WebSocket options, matching Alix-007's pattern in Slack, Discord, Mattermost, xAI, and Signal WebSockets.

## User Impact

Stalled OpenAI realtime voice connections now fail within 10 s during the WebSocket upgrade phase. Healthy connections are unaffected.

## Evidence

### Unit tests

- `openai/realtime-voice-provider.test.ts`: **66/66 passed**.
- `expect(options?.handshakeTimeout).toBe(10_000)` — verifies the constant reaches the constructor.

### ws library contract proof

```json
{"handshakeTimeout_ms":2000,"error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsed_ms":2011,"result":"TIMED_OUT"}
{"handshakeTimeout_ms":10000,"error":"Opening handshake has timed out","elapsed_ms":10012,"result":"TIMED_OUT"}
```

The production value (10 s) causes the ws library to reject a stalled upgrade within the deadline. The pre-fix default (0) waits indefinitely.

### handshakeTimeout vs bridge watchdog (non-redundant)

| Layer | Guards | Failure mode |
|------|------|------|
| `handshakeTimeout` (ws) | TCP accept → HTTP upgrade | Stalled before `open` event |
| `connectTimeout` (bridge) | WS open → session configured | Stalled after `open` event |

These protect different phases. The bridge watchdog fires `setTimeout(() => ws.terminate(), 10_000)`, but `ws.terminate()` on a socket still in CONNECTING state (stalled upgrade) may not release the underlying TCP fd — the ws library must handle this internally via `handshakeTimeout`.
